questions.question: What does 3PL stand for?
questions.explanation: A 3PL is a Third-Party Logistics company that manages freight and shipping for other businesses.

questions.question: What does a freight broker do?

options.a: Owns trucks and drives every load
options.c: Connects shippers with carriers to move freight, without owning the trucks

questions.explanation: A broker is the middle person: the shipper has freight, the carrier has the truck, and the broker matches and manages the move.

questions.question: Which equipment is used for temperature-controlled freight such as frozen or fresh food?
questions.explanation: A reefer is a refrigerated trailer that keeps freight at a set temperature.

questions.question: Which equipment is best for tall or oversized machinery that cannot fit in a regular trailer?
questions.explanation: A step deck has a lower deck, so it can carry taller freight. A Flatbed is open for freight that needs side or top loading.

questions.question: Which of these is a load board used to find loads and carriers?
questions.explanation: DAT, Truckstop, Sylectus, and Highway are the load boards used in carrier sourcing.

questions.question: Before selecting a carrier, what should you verify?

options.a: Their authority and insurance, and check for identity theft or fraud alerts
options.d: Nothing, if their rate is low

questions.explanation: Always vet the carrier: active authority, insurance, and any identity theft or fraud alerts. A cheap rate from a fake carrier can cost you the whole load.

questions.question: Before you book a load, what must you confirm with the carrier?

options.c: Nothing, you can fix it later
options.d: The rate, pickup and delivery times, equipment, and accessorial terms

questions.explanation: Confirm all terms before booking, then put them on the rate confirmation so there are no surprises later.

questions.question: What is the best way to negotiate a rate with a carrier?

options.a: Know your target and maximum rate, stay professional, and counter with a reason
options.d: Offer a very low price without explaining

questions.explanation: Know your numbers first, stay respectful, and give a reason for your counter. This keeps the relationship and protects your margin.

questions.question: Which document confirms the agreed rate and terms between the broker and the carrier?
questions.explanation: The Rate Confirmation (ratecon) is the carrier's agreement to the rate and terms of the load.

questions.question: What does a COI (Certificate of Insurance) prove?

options.b: That the carrier has valid insurance coverage

questions.explanation: The COI shows the carrier's insurance coverage and is part of the carrier packet.

questions.question: The load is covered. What do you do on the dispatch call?

options.a: Ask for the driver's home address
options.d: Confirm he is empty, get his ETA, and confirm all is set for pickup

questions.explanation: Dispatching means calling the driver to confirm he is empty, get his ETA, and make sure everything is ready for pickup.

questions.question: You learn the truck will be late. What is the best move?

options.a: Tell the customer early with the new ETA and next step
options.b: Wait until the delivery is missed

questions.explanation: Bad news early. Customers trust you more when you tell them first, with a clear ETA and next step.

questions.question: What is detention?

options.a: A fee for a cancelled load after the truck arrives
options.b: A fee for using a liftgate
options.c: A fee when the driver waits too long at pickup or delivery after the free time
options.d: A fee for an extra stop

questions.explanation: Detention is a waiting-time fee charged after the free time, usually 2 hours.

questions.question: What does TONU stand for?
questions.explanation: TONU is Truck Ordered Not Used: the truck came, but the load was cancelled or not ready.

questions.question: Why is a clean POD important before closing the load?

options.a: No POD means no billing, and the customer will not pay
options.c: It is only for the driver

questions.explanation: The POD is proof of delivery. Without it you cannot bill correctly, so the load cannot be closed properly.
